briefs.audience: college students new to board games
briefs.subject: Inviting overhead view of a communal table with a simple generic board game, mugs, dice, and empty chairs, with space to join. No people. Editorial flat illustration, not a photo.
copy: New to game night? So are we.
Meet friendly hosts who love easy games and low-pressure evenings.
A weekly board-game night for students at our college. Make room for one more.
styles: Bauhaus modernism: functional sans serif, clear hierarchy, circle-square-triangle geometry, organized asymmetric grid. Cream, vermilion, black, a little golden yellow. Main text LEFT and circular table illustration RIGHT, CTA beneath copy. Inspired by Herbert Bayer's geometric Bauhaus exhibition graphic, original content.

Punk postmodern counter-design: hand-cut typography in legible uneven strips, photocopied illustration, torn paper, tape and xerox grain. Hot pink, acid yellow and deep black, no cream modernist grid. Table illustration LEFT, staggered copy RIGHT, CTA on solid yellow band. DIY welcoming zine, not aggressive or exclusionary. Inspired by Jamie Reid's cut-and-paste method, not monarchy imagery.

briefs.audience: college study groups who want a short playful break
briefs.subject: A fan of playful generic game cards, a comically bent pencil, a smiling geometric shape and dice, visually funny but clear product preview. No people. Editorial flat illustration, not photo.
copy: For friends who love bad puns and quick laughs. Take a playful study break.
Our study group. Our silly ritual.
Turn your group's study break into a shared game. Keep the inside jokes going.
styles: De Stijl modernism: strict horizontal and vertical black rules, unequal rectangles, pure red blue yellow with large white spaces. No diagonal decorative lines, no squiggles. Headline in large top-left white block, illustration in lower-right yellow block, CTA separate red rectangle. Refer to Mondrian's Composition in Red Blue and Yellow via orthogonal structure; original product art.

Memphis postmodernism: exuberant lavender, turquoise, tangerine and hot pink, playful stacked geometric forms, black squiggles, dots, intentionally clashing patterns. Offset illustration upper-left, headline right, clear copy and CTA bottom on plain turquoise panel. Adapt Carlton's playful geometric stacking and laminate-like pattern, not a furniture image.

briefs.audience: adult couples looking for an unhurried shared evening
briefs.offer: Free printable conversation cards for two.
briefs.subject: Exactly two tea cups with gentle steam beside a small fan of blank conversation cards, a quiet table and one small flower. No people. Flat editorial illustration with paper texture; do not make a photographic living room.
copy: For people who love slow evenings.
We love good tea and unhurried conversation, too. Make a little time for each other.
A little ritual for the two of us.
Make time for the bond you share. Keep your story growing, one conversation at a time.
styles: Mid-Century modernist graphic design: flat cut-paper organic silhouettes, asymmetric balance, generous negative space, simple serif paired with clean sans. Warm cream, terracotta, olive and cocoa. Text on left, simplified two-cup illustration on right. Adapt Saul Bass's economical cut-paper shapes, not his film imagery. No realistic interiors.

Push Pin eclectic illustration in contrast to restrained modernism: bold outlined whimsical two-cup drawing, looping steam shaped into a subtle heart, expressive readable decorative serif headline, hand-drawn floral border. Deep aubergine, rose, peach and pale gold, not cream/olive. Illustration on left, expressive headline right, body on plain pale-pink panel, deep aubergine CTA. Original decorative editorial illustration with historical-lettering flavor and visual metaphor; not psychedelic illegibility.
